newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Soundwill seen in HK$600-795 mln share float.
newsitem.headline: HK's Soundwill seen in HK$600-795 mln share float.

text.p: Property redeveloper Soundwill Holdings Ltd is expected to raise HK$600 million to $795 million in an initial public offer (IPO) to fund property investment and redevelopment projects in Hong Kong, market sources said on Friday.
Soundwill is expected to issue 300 million new shares, or 25 percent of its share capital, at a price ranging from HK$2.00 to HK$2.65 per share, market sources said.
"The issue price will represent a 21 to 38 percent discount to NAV (net asset value) and it gives a P/E (price/earnings ratio) of about 20 times," said one analyst.
About 85 percent of the issue will be for international placement and 15 percent will be offered to the public in Hong Kong, they said.
The Hong Kong IPO will run from March 10 to 13, with the price to be fixed on March 18, and dealing in shares is expected to begin on March 21, the sources said.
ING Baring is expected to be the sponsor of the issue.

"Soundwill estimates a profit of HK$127 million for the year ended in December 1996, up from HK$115 million in 1995," the analyst said. "It recorded a profit of HK$28 million for the nine months ended in September 1996."
The analyst said profit from sales of property during the fourth quarter last year boosted its overall profit for 1996.
Soundwill reported a profit of HK$233 million in 1993 but only HK$93 million in 1994, the analyst said.
Among the proceeds, about HK$239 million will be used to fund its purchase of property, HK$108 million for loan repayment and the balance for working capital, the sources said.
Soundwill engages in property investment and redevelopment in Hong Kong, particularly in the commercial property sector in Causeway Bay district on Hong Kong Island.
